column1: 10-3 Aggregate Demand Aggregate demand (AD) is the relationship between the quantity of output demanded and the aggregate price level. In other words, the aggregate demand curve tells us the quantity of goods and services people want to buy at any given level of prices. We examine the theory of aggregate demand in detail in Chapters 11 through 13. Here we use the quantity theory of money to provide a simple, although incomplete, derivation of the aggregate demand curve.
